cards.note: Road 8B is a thin paved road (divided north of Chachapoyas) surrounded by distinct looking mountains. South towards the Cajamarca border the road runs along the edge of the mountain.
Road 106 is a gen 4 dirt road in the Cordillera Blanca and is one of the most beautiful and easily recognizable roads in Peru.
Road 1N in Ancash (and parts of Lima) passes through a sandy desert landscape. A divided highway through desert with sand dunes is a good indicator of Ancash region.
Very foggy roads can be found in Ancash region, in the mountains west of Yungay.
The Ancash/La Libertad border road passes through dry, rocky mountains. Most of the road looks like this. While part of it is two lanes, the majority is a narrow, paved road.
Road 30A cuts through a gorge. The entire road has overcast coverage, giving it a slightly dark appearance. The mountains are very recognizable.
Road 30B is a thin, paved road with distinct-looking pavement, having darker lines a bit like Texas pavement.
Road 3S in Apurimac, the main road between Ayacucho and Cusco, is a winding route along the edge of the mountains. Its elevated position overlooking a valley is a good indicator of Apurimac region.
Road 28B in Ayacucho region looks similar to the one in Cusco as it passes through tropical hills, but this section has road lines, unlike the more recognizable part in Cusco region.
Road 30A, between Nazca and Puquio, is a winding road passing through rugged, dry mountain ranges. Also these bollards are common along this road.
East of Puquio lies a vast, open plain of arid terrain. It is sparsely vegetated with low-lying brown and beige scrub. Much of the coverage is very overcast and appears a bit dark.
Road 30D through central Ayacucho is a thin, paved, high-elevation mountain road. The landscape is very barren, similar to roads in Huancavelica region.
Road 32 near Puquio is a thin mountain road. The northern section is a dirt road, while the southern section is paved. It has some bushes and shrubs, also rock walls are common along this road.
The main roads in northern Cajamarca, near the Ecuador border, are mountainous, and pass through tropical vegetation.
Cusco region has a few smallcam roads passing through the rainforest. Road 113, which leads to Manu National Park, is a narrow paved road surrounded by tropical vegetation.

The 28B is one of the most useful Amazonian roads to learn. The entire road runs along a river valley and has no road lines. Sections of the road are unpaved, but the majority is paved without road lines.

These two roads descend through a valley of big tropical mountains. The roads are in good condition and have lots of bollards as well as yellow-black markings on guardrails. 34B drives north, 30C SW towards Cusco.
If you see steep, rugged brown mountains in a valley, you are probably in the Sacred Valley near Cusco, between Ollantaytambo and Pisac.

This gen 3 coverage, with a white (or almost blurred-out) Google car, very overcast skies, and a wintery feel (often with snow on the mountaintops), is found in southern Cusco region between Sicuani and the Arequipa region border.
Road 14A is a narrow, paved gen 4 road winding through hilly tropical vegetation.
Sandy gen 4 desert roads are most common in Ica region.
This dark asphalt pavement is almost on the entire road to Iquitos as well as in parts of the city, making it the easiest way to recognize the area. All roads in Iquitos are gen 3.
The road to Yurimaguas is mostly flat and tropical. It looks similar to the road to Pucallpa.
Road 30C is a flat, well paved road passing through the rain forest. It has clear skies, unlike most other Amazonian main roads. On the southern section, the sky has an orange tint.
Road 108 is a gen 4 dirt road with sparse arid vegetation, including shrubs, bushes, and some cacti. Snowcapped mountains may also be visible.
Road 36A in Moquegua has an arid landscape with scattered bushes and shrubs. Similar-looking terrain can also be found in Tacna and in south-western Ayacucho regions.
The coastal highway in Moquegua region runs north-south along the ocean and is quite winding.
This unique concrete pavement exists only on Road 18 in Pasco and Lima regions.

The section of the 5N passing through the mountains in Pasco region is a winding, unpaved dirt road (c2023). The only other roads that may look similar are the unpaved sections of the 28B, but the 5N is generally more winding and narrow.
Road 5N towards Pucallpa in Pasco and Huanuco regions is a mostly straight, north-south, flat road in good condition surrounded by tropical vegetation. Use road angle to find the right stretch.
The eastern 1N road between Lambayeque and Piura regions runs straight NNW, with a significant mountain ridge to the east.
The southern part of Road 38 in Puno, which continues into Tacna region, is the only thin, paved gen 4 road in the region.
The only divided road in the region connects Puno and Juliaca.
Road 105, northeast of Tarapoto, is a thin paved road north of the mountains, running east-west through the rainforest.
Road 40 climbs from Tacna to very high elevations, passing through a variety of landscapes. Parts of the route are unpaved, and you can see several volcanoes along the way.
The gen 3 roads through central Tumbes are easy to recognize. They are very dry, with sandy soil and a somewhat savanna-like landscape.
The main road in Tumbes runs parallel to the coast, with ocean to the north. To the south, you often see hills of light-colored, sedimentary soil, which are a good clue for Tumbes region.
Road 5N from Tingo Maria towards Pucallpa is a very winding, somewhat hilly road with tropical vegetation. It looks similar to the road to Yurimaguas, north of Tarapoto.
Road 18C is gen 4, flat, well-paved, and passes through tropical vegetation, sometimes including oil palms.
